description: Fix Problem 3 (real Android runtime permissions) at the native + bridge + manifest layer. The installed APK currently requests NO permissions because MayraAndroidPlugin.requestPermission() is a stub returning {granted:false}. Implement REAL Capacitor 6 runtime permissions for microphone (RECORD_AUDIO), contacts (READ_CONTACTS), and location (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION/ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION), plus an accessibility deep-link path (accessibility cannot be granted by a runtime dialog). Wire android-bridge.js to pass through to the real native methods and expose openAccessibilitySettings, with browser fallbacks preserved. Update AndroidManifest.xml. This feature is independent of FEAT-001/002 (permissions vs API keys) and could be parallelized, but the UI that surfaces these (FEAT-004) depends on it. Kotlin CANNOT be compiled in this sandbox (no Android SDK/network) — verify by careful reading + exact JS<->Kotlin name/param matching.
steps: AndroidManifest.xml (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml): add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION" /> and <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION" /> alongside the existing dangerous permissions. Keep existing RECORD_AUDIO/INTERNET/READ_CONTACTS/POST_NOTIFICATIONS/MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS and the <queries>/FileProvider blocks intact. (A full AccessibilityService <service> with BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE + res/xml config is OPTIONAL/bonus; the deep-link-to-settings path is the required minimum, so a manifest service is not required.)

MayraAndroidPlugin.kt: change the class annotation to declare permission aliases: @CapacitorPlugin(name = "MayraAndroid", permissions = [ @Permission(alias = "microphone", strings = [Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO]), @Permission(alias = "contacts", strings = [Manifest.permission.READ_CONTACTS]), @Permission(alias = "location", strings = [Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, Manifest.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION]) ]). Add the imports: android.Manifest, com.getcapacitor.annotation.Permission, com.getcapacitor.annotation.PermissionCallback, com.getcapacitor.PermissionState.

MayraAndroidPlugin.kt requestPermission(call): REPLACE the stub. Read call.getString("permission") which will be one of 'microphone'|'contacts'|'location'. If getPermissionState(alias) is already GRANTED, resolve {granted:true} immediately. Otherwise call requestPermissionForAlias(alias, call, "permissionCallback"). Add a @PermissionCallback private fun permissionCallback(call: PluginCall) that re-reads the requested alias from the saved call (persist it — e.g. use call.getString("permission") again since Capacitor re-delivers the same call, or store bridge.saveCall) and resolves {granted: getPermissionState(alias) == PermissionState.GRANTED}. Ensure the granted boolean reflects the REAL OS result. Handle an unknown/blank alias by rejecting or resolving {granted:false} without crashing.

MayraAndroidPlugin.kt checkPermission(call): add a new @PluginMethod fun checkPermission(call) that reads 'permission' ('microphone'|'contacts'|'location'), maps to the alias, and resolves { status: <'granted'|'denied'|'prompt'> } derived from getPermissionState(alias) (GRANTED->'granted', DENIED->'denied', PROMPT/PROMPT_WITH_RATIONALE->'prompt'). This gives android-bridge.checkPermission a real native status source.

MayraAndroidPlugin.kt accessibility: add @PluginMethod fun openAccessibilitySettings(call) that starts Intent(android.provider.Settings.ACTION_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS) (with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK if launched from non-activity context) and resolves success. Add @PluginMethod fun isAccessibilityEnabled(call) that reports whether THIS app's accessibility service is enabled — read Settings.Secure.getString(contentResolver, Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES) and check if it contains the app package name; resolve { enabled: Boolean }. (If no AccessibilityService class is shipped, this will report false until the user enables one; that is acceptable per the minimum spec — document it.)

Keep openApp/openUrl/makeCall/callContact/openSettings EXACTLY as they are (they are real and working). Only add/modify requestPermission, add checkPermission, openAccessibilitySettings, isAccessibilityEnabled.

js/android-bridge.js requestPermission(permName): keep the native pass-through (bridge.requestPermission({permission: permName}) -> result.granted) as the primary path for 'microphone'|'contacts'|'location'. Extend the web fallback: microphone via getUserMedia (as today); ADD location fallback via navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition (resolve true on success position, false on error) or navigator.permissions.query({name:'geolocation'}); contacts + accessibility remain unavailable on web (return false). Do not remove existing behavior.

js/android-bridge.js checkPermission(permName): route through the native bridge first when available — call bridge.checkPermission({permission: permName}) and return result.status. Keep the existing navigator.permissions web fallback for microphone; add a geolocation branch for location; return 'unknown' for contacts/accessibility on web.

js/android-bridge.js: add openAccessibilitySettings() that calls bridge.openAccessibilitySettings() when native, else App.showToast a warm message that accessibility must be enabled from the device's Accessibility settings manually. Add isAccessibilityEnabled() that calls bridge.isAccessibilityEnabled() -> result.enabled when native, else returns false. Add BOTH new methods to the AndroidBridge returned public API object at the bottom.

Consistency check: the JS permission name strings ('microphone','contacts','location') passed by android-bridge.js MUST exactly match the Kotlin aliases; the JS method names openAccessibilitySettings/isAccessibilityEnabled and their result field names ({granted}, {status}, {enabled}) MUST exactly match what the Kotlin @PluginMethods resolve.

Verify: `unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check js/android-bridge.js`; validate AndroidManifest.xml is well-formed XML; carefully re-read MayraAndroidPlugin.kt confirming imports, annotation aliases, @PermissionCallback wiring, and that method names/params/result keys match android-bridge.js exactly.
acceptance_criteria: AndroidManifest.xml is well-formed XML and declares ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION in addition to the pre-existing permissions; existing <queries> and FileProvider are intact.

MayraAndroidPlugin.kt no longer has a stub requestPermission; @CapacitorPlugin declares @Permission aliases microphone/contacts/location; requestPermission uses getPermissionState + requestPermissionForAlias with a @PermissionCallback and resolves {granted:true|false} from the real OS state.
MayraAndroidPlugin.kt exposes checkPermission (resolving {status}), openAccessibilitySettings, and isAccessibilityEnabled (resolving {enabled}).

android-bridge.js requestPermission/checkPermission pass through to the native methods for microphone/contacts/location and keep web fallbacks (mic getUserMedia, location geolocation, contacts/accessibility unavailable on web); openAccessibilitySettings and isAccessibilityEnabled are added to the AndroidBridge public export.
JS permission-name strings and JS method/result-field names match the Kotlin aliases and @PluginMethod signatures EXACTLY.
verification: grep the Kotlin @Permission aliases and the JS permName strings; confirm 'microphone'/'contacts'/'location' match on both sides
grep openAccessibilitySettings and isAccessibilityEnabled in both js/android-bridge.js and MayraAndroidPlugin.kt and confirm identical names + result field keys ({granted}/{status}/{enabled})
findings: Implemented real Capacitor 6 runtime permissions. AndroidManifest.xml: added ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION + ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION (existing perms/queries/FileProvider untouched, XML well-formed). MayraAndroidPlugin.kt: @CapacitorPlugin now declares @Permission aliases microphone(RECORD_AUDIO)/contacts(READ_CONTACTS)/location(ACCESS_FINE+COARSE); added imports android.Manifest, android.provider.Settings, com.getcapacitor.PermissionState, com.getcapacitor.annotation.Permission, com.getcapacitor.annotation.PermissionCallback. requestPermission stub REPLACED: returns {granted:true} immediately if already GRANTED, else requestPermissionForAlias(alias, call, "permissionCallback"); @PermissionCallback permissionCallback re-reads alias from re-delivered call and resolves {granted:<real OS state>}. Unknown/blank alias resolves {granted:false} (no crash) via isKnownAlias() helper. Added @PluginMethod checkPermission -> {status:'granted'|'denied'|'prompt'} (PROMPT/PROMPT_WITH_RATIONALE both map to 'prompt'). Added openAccessibilitySettings (Intent ACTION_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS + FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK on context) resolving {success:true}, and isAccessibilityEnabled reading Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES and checking for packageName -> {enabled:Boolean}. NOTE: no AccessibilityService class is shipped, so isAccessibilityEnabled reports false until the user enables one manually (acceptable per minimum spec; deep-link path is the required minimum). openApp/openUrl/makeCall/callContact/openSettings left byte-for-byte unchanged. js/android-bridge.js: requestPermission keeps native pass-through (result.granted) and adds a location web fallback via navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition (contacts/accessibility return false on web, mic getUserMedia unchanged). checkPermission now routes through native bridge.checkPermission({permission}) -> result.status first, with navigator.permissions web fallbacks for microphone and geolocation (location), 'unknown' for contacts/accessibility. Added openAccessibilitySettings() (native call, else warm Hinglish toast) and isAccessibilityEnabled() (native result.enabled, else false); both added to the AndroidBridge public export. Cross-language consistency verified by grep: aliases and method/result-key names match exactly. Kotlin NOT compiled (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, no Android SDK) — verified by careful reading + name/param/result-key matching. Static verification passed: `node --check js/android-bridge.js` OK, AndroidManifest.xml well-formed. Did NOT commit (orchestrator commits).
